items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: Analog Africa厂牌再次聚焦贝宁传奇乐团Orchestre Poly-Rythmo，本辑汇集1977至1982年间与歌手兼作曲者Antoine Dougbé的合作录音。Dougbé以拍击大腿的Cavacha节奏为核心创作手法，结合巫毒传统音乐语汇，与鼓手Belobi Meridjo发源自火车节奏的律动共同塑造了这批作品的声音骨架。乐评指出这批录音的音色已显露出年代过渡特征——吉他带有塑料光泽、合成器开始进入编制，古巴son的影响在开篇几首尤为突出，刚果伦巴的律动也清晰可辨。Dougbé本人以'魔鬼首相'的称号闻名，对演奏者要求严苛，只与Poly-Rythmo长期合作，短暂的录音生涯留下三张专辑与若干单曲，本辑将这些作品汇集，呈现出一段融合巫毒仪式感、非洲放克与拉丁元素的独特历史切片。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组的首张数字EP，共收录五首曲目，以北欧民间音乐为底色，融合口簧琴、风笛、钦巴龙、长笛和弦乐等传统乐器，营造出一种古老而粗粝的氛围。主唱Mia Guldhammer的嗓音具有说服力，既能展现粗犷奔腾的节奏感，也能在抒情段落中呈现柔软质感。乐队成员Morten Musicus贡献了唯一一首原创作品，其余多为民俗传统的重新诠释。编曲注重乐器间的纹理交织，器乐尾曲在口簧琴、长笛与弦乐的对话中展现出不安分而令人兴奋的实验性。作为北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手主导项目，乐队虽刚出道却展现出超越新人的成熟度，但整体仍偏向传统民谣范畴，在实验性突破方面尚有空间。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the major players of the 21st century folk revival scene, JOANNA NEWSOM has foundinternational fame with her unique musical performances that includes intricate harp instrumentationand a very unusual quirky vocal style. While her album "Ys" would propel to folk royalty, her debutrelease THE MILK-EYED MENDER was met with positive critique and universal love as well. NEWSOM grewup in Grass Valley, California and is actually distantly related to the state's governor. NEWSOM wasgifted with a rather quick ascent to fame after only appearing as a guest musician on a Nervous Copalbum before setting out on her own and capturing the folk world's attention in record time. After acouple warmup EPs, she has released four critically acclaimed albums so far.THE MILK-EYED MENDER was NEWSOM's debut which not only showcased her multi-instrumental talents thatincluded harpsichord, piano, keyboards and harp but also featured her unique songwriting styles thathad one foot in the catchy world of pop music while maintaining an authentic medieval feel detachedfrom the modern day excesses of production and technology overload. This is a solo album frombeginning to end with NEWSOM performing every instrumental and having written and sung every song.While "Ys" would evolve NEWSOM's sound into a more complex orchestral production, THE MILK-EYEDMENDER is the perfect place to inure your musical sensibilities to NEWSOM's bizarre sounding vocalidiosyncrasies.The album features 12 tracks that add up to just over 52 minutes and all written by NEWSOM herselfexcept the traditional folk song "Three Little Babies." The album indeed comes off as a collectionof child-like songs structured around the harp which plays an interesting role as both the basis forrhythm as well as providing the melodic backing to NEWSOM's lyrical performances. The album alsofeatures both acoustic and electric pianos as well as harpsichord but the album is fairly sparse asfar as instrumentation and showcases NEWSOM's ability to express herself through the barest of bonessimplicity and yet sounding somehow uncannily complete with the harp alone serving as the entireinstrumentation for the majority of the album's run.While the most stripped down and most accessible of NEWSOM's releases that would become moreexperimental after this one's release, THE MILK-EYED MENDER holds up as a well-constructed piece ofharp-based folk music in its own right despite no excursions into the progressive chamber folk thatwould find her embraced by the modern New Weird America culture that found NEWSOM in the company ofthe likes of Devendra Barnhart, Animal Collective and Espers. Ironically this strong debut wouldprove to only be the beginning for NEWSOM who quickly captured the momentum and expanded herambitions into the world of more complex progressive arenas. Many may find this a bit too naive andinnocent in comparison to the grandiosity of "Ys" however it's exactly the bare bones authenticitythat i find appealing about this debut which establishes NEWSOM as a talent in her own right beforegoing into more adventurous collaborative efforts.
items._genre: prog folk / harp folk / chamber folk
items._cn_summary: 这是Joanna Newsom的首张专辑，以竖琴为核心乐器贯穿全作，辅以钢琴、大键琴与键盘，构筑出极简的器乐框架。她独自完成所有器乐演奏与词曲创作，12首曲目中仅一首为传统民歌改编。整张专辑呈现出中世纪民谣的质朴气质，与当代过度制作形成鲜明对比，嗓音具有独特的怪趣质感。她的声音在民谣复兴场景中独树一帜，既保留了流行旋律的亲和力，又保持着未经现代技术修饰的原始感。作为她后续更为宏大管弦乐作品的前奏，这张专辑是最为质朴易入门的起点，展现了她以最少器乐编配表达完整音乐意涵的能力。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — Like neighboring Spain, the Portuguese prog scene was stifled along with other artistic innovationsdue to the stranglehold dictatorship known as the Estado Novo which retained its iron grip until the1974 Carnation Revolution which at long last brought Portugal into the modern world. While artistswere prevented from offering their free expression, they were certainly aware of the developmentsthroughout the rest of Europe however two bands didn't wait for the revolution to unfold but rathergot the prog party started before the big change. The first was Quarteto 1111 and following suit in1971 was PESTRUS CASTRUS formed by brothers Pedro Castro and Jos� Castro, the former of whom servedas the band's moniker albeit in a Latinized form. The brothers recruited Julio Pereira (guitars) andRui Reis (keyboards) from the band Play Boys and eventually drummer Jo�o Seixas. Unlike Quarteto1111 though, PESTRUS CASTRUS began as a prog band from the very start albeit one was more crossoverin nature bridging the psychedelic rock 60s with the more elaborately designed prog that wassweeping the world by 1973.The band spawned two EPs, "Marasmo" and "Tudo Isto, Tudo Mais" as tantalizing warmups but alreadymastered the art of catchy melodic hooks cradled in the symphonic prog stylistic approach of theera. The first debut full-length followed in 1973. MESTRE ("Master") was a latecomer to the overallprog game by barely making it out in 1973 released in December but formerly announced Portugal wasready to join the rest of the world and as a result MESTRE is considered the very first Portugueseprog album which boldly emerged before the Estado Novo had even crumbled and unsurprisingly wascompletely banned by the Censorship Commission. And it's no wonder as the lyrics (in Portuguese)were confrontational and challenged the government directly by including adapted works of Portugueseand Brazilian antiestablishment poets that included Alexandre O'Neill, Fernando Pessoa, Sophia deMello Breyner Andresen, Manuel Bandeira, and Bocage.Stylistically MESTRE is quite diverse hosting a collection of 11 tracks that run the gamut ofkeyboard-oriented symphonic prog, 60s psychedelic rock and contemplative folk with strong melodicdevelopments. While the style is somewhat similar to the symphonic prog of Italian artists, PESTRUSCASTRUS wasn't as technically proficient nor were the compositions steeped in classical overtones.The basis for the song structures is clearly more steeped in 60s psychedelic scenes only adapted tothe symphonic sensibilities that were en vogue in the early 1970s. The Beatles was a clear influenceon the melodic hooks as well as the occasional delving into the McCartney'esque vaudeville styledshow tune "Macaco" while "S.A.R.L" takes on a Santana-styled Latin rock vibe. Despite these outliersthough the album is primarily steeped with rather nonchalant contemplative symphonic rock tracksthat bring the more atmospheric moments of PFM or Banco to mind.Overall MESTRE is a dramatic take on melodic symphonic prog that may prove to be to mainstreamsounding for many but when taken into context with the barriers put in place for albums like this toemerge in the first place, it's an absolute testament of fortitude that this album was released asearly as it was. Perhaps not the masterpiece many have touted it as but surely an excellent slice ofmelodic symphonic prog polished with a fiery passion fueled by a perception that freedom was justaround the corner. While the Portuguese language may be a barrier for lyrical comprehension formany, the music itself is well worth the price of admission with beautifully constructed songs thatevoke all the wild mood swings of a classic prog album from the era. The band would go on hiatus forseveral years with the two brothers studying abroad to earn degrees in economics and engineering,the band returned in 1979 to release one more album "Ascen��o e Queda" before calling it quits forgood. While the band never achieved any significant success, it has indeed become legendary on thePortuguese prog scene.
items._genre: symphonic prog / psychedelic rock / folk / latin rock
items._cn_summary: 这张1973年的葡萄牙专辑被视为该国首张真正意义上的前卫摇滚作品，在独裁政权的审查制度尚未崩溃前即已诞生，歌词直接收录了多位葡语反建制诗人的作品，因此遭禁。乐队由Pedro Castro兄弟领军，从60年代迷幻摇滚与早期交响前卫的交汇处出发，融合了键盘主导的交响段落、迷幻摇滚段落以及沉思型的民谣段落。专辑收录11首曲目，风格跨度相当广，Beatles式的旋律钩子、McCartney风格的杂耍式小曲、Santana式的拉丁律动交替出现，同时也展现了PFM与Banco那种氛围化的交响摇滚肌理。相比意大利同侪，技术精湛度与古典底蕴略逊，但歌词的政治锋芒与时代语境使其具有超出音乐本身的文献价值。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — 'The Piper At the Gates of Dawn' is the 1967 debut album by British rock band Pink Floyd. I always thought I was fine with experimental music, that I was open-minded enough to enjoy music that deviates from traditional songwriting practices. But perhaps I was wrong, because this album is completely and utterly "out there", and my delicate senses just can't cope. Somehow, Pink Floyd went from this album to eventually becoming one of the biggest bands in history, but I've yet to figure out how. I give them credit for completely throwing out the rulebook and thinking outside the box, but that doesn't necessarily mean these songs are actually any good. Because I find them boring as hell. The only one that remotely stands out to me, is 'The Gnome', but there's no way I'm going out of my way to listen to it. These might have been revolutionary and exciting back in the 1960's, but that's way ahead of my time, and by today's standards, I'll be having none of this. Still, regardless of this debut, Pink Floyd really are one of the biggest bands of all time, so I'll continue on my personal Floyd journey, and will see what their next album has in store for me.
items._cn_summary: 这是Pink Floyd 1967年发行的首张专辑，评论者坦言自己在面对实验音乐时感到无所适从。整张专辑被描述为完全跳出传统创作规则的作品，音域探索在当时具有革命性。评论者认为专辑中的歌曲对他而言极为乏味，唯有《The Gnome》稍能引起注意。作为Syd Barrett主导时期的产物，专辑承载了英国地下迷幻文化的早期精神，歌曲结构松散、声音处理怪诞、歌词充满超现实意象。尽管评论者对这张处女作评价不高，但他承认Pink Floyd后来确实成为摇滚史上最具影响力的乐队之一，并决定继续探索他们后续的作品。

items.body: Los Angeles industrial/EBM act Frontal Boundary released “Alone EP” on 11 September 2026 through Alfa Matrix. The 8-track digital EP opens the door to the band’s forthcoming album “Shattered Mind”. The tracklist runs “Alone”, a cover of Garbage’s “Milk” featuring Kimber Parrish, an alternate version of “Alone”, and five remixes of the title track: by Assemblage 23, Protokoll 19, Reaper, Asphodel Ivory and The Axiom Divide. Alone EP by Frontal Boundary The title track explores isolation and grief, moving Frontal Boundary’s established dark electro toward more melodic, emotionally exposed songwriting. The five remixers each take “Alone” in a different direction, from Assemblage 23‘s atmospheric treatment to the harder electronic versions from Protokoll 19 and Reaper and the more experimental readings by Asphodel Ivory and The Axiom Divide. Frontal Boundary’s run on Alfa Matrix “Alone EP” follows a string of Alfa Matrix releases from the band. Frontal Boundary signed to the label in July 2025 with the “Hate” EP, followed by the 8-track “Faith” EP in September 2025 and the full-length album “Failure” on 12 December 2025, released as a digital edition and a limited 2CD set. The band closed out the “Failure” cycle with the 7-track “Burn” EP, featuring a cover of Filter’s “Hey Man Nice Shot”, on 24 April 2026. “Alone EP” is the band’s first release of the “Shattered Mind” era. About Frontal Boundary Frontal Boundary is a Los Angeles-based industrial/EBM project formed by Brendin Ross (ex-Bile, Dawn Of Ashes, Bornless Fire) in 2008. The project issued the demo “Never Ending” and the debut track “Mindfuck” in 2009, then released its first album, “Electronic Warfare”, on 6 January 2012, followed by a 2013 re-release as “Electronic Warfare V.2”. Ross toured the project alongside acts including God Module and Suicide Commando during this period. Vocalist Krz Souls (Dawn Of Ashes, Bornless Fire) joined in 2019, and the pair released the album “The Fall” on 19 March 2021. Synth player Jaysen Craves (Livernois) joined as a full member in 2023, the year Frontal Boundary signed to Re:Mission Entertainment. That signing led to the singles “Shutting Down” and “Without A Chance” and the album “Shutting Down” on 27 September 2024, followed by the remix collection “Shutting Down Remixed” in April 2025 and the “Hollow” EP with Unter Null in March 2025. Frontal Boundary moved to Alfa Matrix in 2025, releasing “Hate”, “Faith” and the album “Failure” before the “Burn” EP in April 2026. “Alone EP” continues that run and leads into the band’s fifth full-length album, “Shattered Mind”.
items._cn_summary: 本文是洛杉矶工业/EBM团体Frontal Boundary新EP的新闻稿式介绍。作品以"Alone EP"为标题,共8首数字曲目,作为即将发行的全长专辑"Shattered Mind"的前导。EP标题曲探讨孤独与悲恸,乐风从乐团此前偏暗的dark electro进一步转向更旋律化、情感外露的写作。收录Garbage名曲"Milk"的翻唱版,由Kimber Parrish献声,另有Assemblage 23、Protokoll 19、Reaper等五位电子音乐人各自诠释的重混版本,涵盖氛围化处理、硬派电子与实验性解构等不同方向。Alfa Matrix为比利时独立厂牌,深耕工业/EBM领域。文章以乐队发展简史作为补充信息,并未对音乐本身做出深度评论,属典型发行通告。

items.body: Ultravox released their fifth studio album, “Rage in Eden,” on 11 September 1981 through Chrysalis Records. The British new wave band recorded the nine-track album with producer Conny Plank at his studio near Cologne, West Germany, following the commercial breakthrough of “Vienna” a year earlier. “Rage in Eden” turns 45 this year. Where the “Vienna” sessions had been rehearsed live before the band entered the studio, Ultravox spent three months making “Rage in Eden,” building songs directly out of studio experiments; the title track grew from a backwards playback of vocals recorded for “I Remember (Death in the Afternoon).” The album runs 45 minutes and 34 seconds across nine tracks: “The Voice,” “We Stand Alone,” “Rage in Eden,” “I Remember (Death in the Afternoon),” “The Thin Wall,” “Stranger Within,” “Accent on Youth,” “The Ascent” and “Your Name (Has Slipped My Mind Again),” with the final three forming a continuous sequence on side two. Warren Cann (drums, electronic percussion, vocals), Chris Cross (bass, synthesizers, vocals), Billy Currie (synthesizers, piano, violin, viola) and Midge Ure (lead vocals, guitars, synthesizers) wrote and performed every song, with the original sleeve designed by Peter Saville Associates. Two singles from the album, “The Thin Wall” and “The Voice,” reached number 14 and number 16 on the UK singles chart, while the album itself peaked at number 4 and was certified Gold by the BPI. “Rage in Eden” streams on Spotify. About Ultravox Ultravox formed in London in April 1974 as Tiger Lily, led by Royal College of Art student Dennis Leigh, later known as John Foxx, alongside Chris Allen, later Chris Cross, on bass and Stevie Shears on guitar, joined that year by drummer Warren Cann and violinist Billy Currie. After several name changes the band signed to Island Records in 1976 and settled on Ultravox!, with the exclamation mark a reference to the krautrock band Neu!, while finishing its 1977 debut, “Ultravox!,” produced by Steve Lillywhite and Brian Eno. “Ha! Ha! Ha!” followed later that year, and 1978’s “Systems of Romance,” produced by Conny Plank, brought synthesizers to the front of the band’s sound. Island dropped Ultravox at the end of 1978, and John Foxx left in March 1979 to pursue a solo career. Midge Ure, previously of Slik and the Rich Kids and a touring member of Thin Lizzy, joined as vocalist, guitarist and keyboardist after collaborating with Billy Currie in the studio project Visage. The reshaped band signed to Chrysalis Records, and “Vienna,” released in July 1980 and again produced by Conny Plank, gave Ultravox its commercial breakthrough: the title single reached number 2 on the UK chart in January 1981. “Rage in Eden” followed on 11 September 1981, again recorded with Plank at his Cologne studio, reaching number 4 in the UK and earning a Gold certification from the BPI. Ultravox then worked with producer George Martin on 1982’s “Quartet,” which reached number 6 in the UK and produced four Top 20 singles, before self-producing 1984’s “Lament,” which included the UK number 3 hit “Dancing with Tears in My Eyes.” That November, Midge Ure co-wrote and produced Band Aid’s “Do They Know It’s Christmas?,” and Ultravox performed at Live Aid in 1985. Warren Cann left the band in 1986, and “U-Vox,” recorded with Big Country’s Mark Brzezicki on drums, became the final album of the original run before Ultravox split in 1987. Billy Currie led a new line-up through two further albums, “Revelation” (1993) and “Ingenuity” (1994), before the band dissolved again in 1996. The classic line-up of Cann, Cross, Currie and Ure reformed in 2008 for the “Return to Eden” tour and released the studio album “Brilliant” in May 2012, followed by a run of UK arena dates with Simple Minds that closed with a show at the O2 Arena in November 2013. Bassist Chris Cross died in March 2024, as Side-Line reported at the time. In October 2025, Chrysalis continued the catalogue’s reissue campaign with “The Collection (Deluxe Edition),” gathering the band’s 1980s singles. “Rage in Eden,” the fifth studio album that captured Ultravox at its most exploratory in the Cologne studio, turns 45 this year.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Ultravox第五张录音室专辑《Rage in Eden》发行45周年的回顾性新闻稿，介绍该专辑于1981年在西德科隆Conny Plank工作室录制，由四名成员共同创作。与前作《Vienna》的现场预演后进棚模式不同，本张专辑耗时三个月，直接从录音棚实验中生发歌曲，标题曲源自另一首歌人声的倒放处理。专辑九首曲目共45分34秒，融合合成器、电子打击乐、提琴与吉他，后三首构成连续的连续段落。封面由Peter Saville Associates设计，两支单曲打入英国单曲榜前二十，专辑获得BPI金认证。文章同时概述了乐队从Tiger Lily到Ultravox!的演变历史，以及Midge Ure取代John Foxx担任主唱的过程。

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑将爵士、激进摇滚与电子元素熔于一炉，参与者来自Trap Music Orchestra、Murderpact、CGI Jesus和Deli Girls等多支地下乐队。评论以美剧《亚特兰大》第三季中Paper Boi嗑药后坠入荒诞现实的桥段作为切入点，暗喻整张专辑所营造的迷幻、扭曲且带有黑色幽默的听感。音乐将爵士的即兴骨架与前卫摇滚的沉重音墙碰撞，产生令人困惑的化学反应。专辑名字'Un-Jazz'本身即是对流派的解构，'New Jazz'被定义为一种脱离传统规则的新物种。然而原文篇幅极短，实质性的音乐分析几乎缺失，仅停留在概念层面的引介，难以判断其实际音响品质与演奏水准。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Exploring Birdsong?a genre-blending act featuring Lynsey, who also provides vocals for Lifesigns, Kite Parade, Caligula's Horse, and Espera (the backing vocal group for Sleep Token)?is hailed as a reincarnation of Kate Bush. They also flirt with the style of Meer; imagine a female Einar Solberg with a touch of Leprous. Expect stunning melodies and a modern sound?prog for today that bears a slight resemblance to Kyros."Archipelago" opens with jazzy, soulful piano as Linsey's magnificent voice launches a meltingly beautiful ballad that balances delicacy and sensuality. There is a breathtaking ambient break and a dash of synth-pop?complete with strings and echoes of Meer?before the track shifts into a wild outro. "42" follows with a striking djent riff; it is heavy at its core, yet takes the form of synth-pop/electro-rock. Vocals drive this modern metal track, accompanied by siren-like backing vocals?innovative and effective. "Romanticise" leans even further into electro, featuring 80s-style synth pads that bridge the gap between mainstream pop and new wave. It carries an energetic hint of Sleep Token, building to a soaring, distorted hard-rock climax. "Footprints" is a mid-tempo ballad amplified by backing vocals and Linsey's rising vocal range. Whether segueing directly or not, "Arrhythmia" evokes a conceptual feel, characterized by a gentle tone and the lingering presence of ethereal piano and vocals. A sudden, sultry solo, a searching spoken-word passage, and a measured riff set against backing vocals enchant the space with crystalline harmonics. "Spy In The House Of Love" arrives with the solemn sound of Celtic bagpipes. It features danceable pop keyboards, an infectious groove, and a vibe reminiscent of XTC?it has it all. An 80s throwback explodes in the chorus?an addictive hook that begs to be sung along to."I_You" features subtle undertones of Coldplay; it is quintessential modern pop with a mainstream touch, yet it navigates prog territory with strings and backing vocals that recall Kate Bush. A sonic extravaganza that invites you to headbang. "The Warning" begins with the intimate folk atmosphere of Scandinavian lands; a somber melody cut through by a hard-hitting synth riff, with backing vocals amplifying the intensity. Strings heighten the drama of lyrics questioning whether to stay together or not. A vulnerable vocal performance carries a weight that flirts with decadent gothic styles. The guitars?and eventually the synths?become frenzied; simply sublime. "You Like It Best When It Hurts" follows a similar vein, bolstered by aggressive synths that evoke modern synth-prog. The riff drives forward with a heavy, rapid-fire attack that beautifully blends with ethereal keyboards. That imaginative guitar riff and the vocal harmonies are spellbinding. "Cartography" returns to the band's roots, with echoes of Kate Bush in this romantic piano ballad featuring a divine vocal performance by Lynsey. "Every House We Built" features a synth sound reminiscent of Tangerine Dream. A vocal-led crescendo builds?exploring themes of relationships and guilt?leading to an infectious drop akin to Brian Eno's work, followed by an expressive rise. "Meadowlands" is a ballad that ebbs and flows with the vocals and fresh, sparkling piano. Airy synths guide the track through a "soft-heavy" prog style, building toward a pop-infused chorus featuring the band Meer, culminating in a fiery finale before a cinematic piano outro.Exploring Birdsong delivers a thrilling fusion of pop, rock, hard synth, and progressive music worthy of Meer.(4.75)
items._genre: crossover prog / synth-pop / electro-rock / progressive metal
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Lynsey领衔，她同时参与多个前卫摇滚项目，乐队被比作Kate Bush与Leprous的交汇点。整体风格在抒情钢琴民谣、合成器流行、电摇、djent金属与新浪潮之间频繁切换，每首歌都试图融合不同元素：爵士钢琴开场后转入合成流行与狂野结尾，djent riff搭配电子摇滚框架，凯尔特风笛与八十年代复古副歌并存，氛围段落与硬摇滚高潮交替出现。编曲层面弦乐、和声层与合成器堆叠丰富，Lynsey的演唱被反复强调为人声核心。但从描述来看，这些融合更接近主流前卫摇滚常见的风格拼接，而非真正具有实验性的声音探索，与实验前卫、自由爵士、电子抽象或暗潮等用户偏好领域的交集有限。评论信息较为完整，但专辑最终曲目描述被截断。

items.body: “Cuando voy a la montaña, voy a mí“, sings Ana María Vahos on “Nuevos Horizontes”: going to the mountain is going to herself, and to a home unlike anywhere else. The mountain she names is home to Horizontes, a village of 195 people at 2,250 metres in the hills northwest of Medellín, where the houses carry their owners’ names on the front instead of street numbers. Vahos’s parents and grandparents lived there, and Sebastián Gómez Agudelo shot the video between the village and Medellín, following her through the streets and among her family. Born in San Pedro de los Milagros in 1993 and based in Medellín, Vahos writes and performs as a cantautora in a guitar-and-voice format, with the 2022 album Los Días behind her. She sings for El Búho, the recording name of Robin Perkins, who grew up in northern England, studied Latin American Studies in Glasgow, lived in Argentina and Mexico City, and started the label Shika Shika with Argentine producer Barrio Lindo in 2015. “Nuevos Horizontes” is the second single from Hogar, out 18 September on Shika Shika, an album Perkins built around field recordings of his own home life, of travel, of islands and of long evenings with friends. Hogar comes down from Latin focus, the fire in the middle of the house. The word for a home started out naming the fire it was built around. He made the record while putting down roots in France for the first time, and Vahos sings about the opposite journey: home as the place you go back to. Perkins hosts a listening party for the album on 13 September. Listen to “Nuevos Horizontes” HERE and pre-order your copy of Hogar following THIS LINK The post Daily Discovery: El Búho – Nuevos Horizontes Feat. Ana María Vahos appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以"家"为主题的概念专辑，由英国电子音乐人Robin Perkins（艺名El Búho）操刀制作。整张专辑围绕田野录音展开，采集了家居生活、旅途、海岛与友人相聚等声音素材，在法国安顿新生活的同时完成创作。哥伦比亚创作歌手Ana MaríaVahos参与了这首单曲的演唱，她的歌词以家乡的山村Horizontes为意象，唱出归乡之路的眷恋。歌曲采用原声吉他与人声的结构，旋律温暖而抒情，Vahos的声线在Perkins的电子氛围编织下显得亲密而私密。专辑在小众独立厂牌Shika Shika发行，带有田野录音与世界音乐元素的融合气质，但整体风格偏向民谣底色，对实验与前卫口味的听众来说创新性较为温和。

items.body: Italian electro-wave project TourdeForce releases a music video for “A Good Death”, a track from the band’s album “Leaving Nothing Left Behind,” released via My Owl Music on 27 February 2026. The video was filmed on location in Japan. “This video represents a watershed and introduces a new era,” TourdeForce’s Christian Ryder stated. The band plans to follow it within a month with a new single and video featuring lead singer Neviah Luneville on vocals. About TourdeForce TourdeForce is an Italian electro-wave and electro-pop project whose recent work Side-Line has followed closely. The band released the album “Vargtimmar” in December 2020, followed by two tribute singles to Death In June: “Six in the Key of Death” in January 2022 and a cover of “The Calling” with an accompanying video in March 2022, before revisiting older material on the compilation “Compendium vol. 1” that June. In April 2025, the project released a single paying tribute to the defunct EKP label. TourdeForce returned in February 2026 with the full-length album “Leaving Nothing Left Behind”, followed in March by an official video for the “LNLB” single mix. “A Good Death” is the latest video from that album, with a new single featuring vocalist Neviah Luneville expected next.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章是一篇纯新闻稿性质的内容，介绍了意大利电子浪潮项目 TourdeForce 发布的音乐录像及作品背景。核心信息集中在新单曲《A Good Death》及其专辑《Leaving Nothing Left Behind》的发行动态，以及后续新单曲和主唱 Neviah Luneville 加入的合作计划。文章还简述了乐队自2020年以来的发行轨迹，包括向 Death In June 致敬的作品、选辑以及向已解散的 EKP 厂牌致敬的单曲。文章本身缺乏任何音乐分析、声音设计讨论或艺术评价，仅作为动态播报存在。对该用户而言，项目所属的电子浪潮与暗潮领域与个人偏好有交集，但内容未触及任何实验性、前卫性或跨界融合层面的探讨，信息密度和深度均不足以形成有价值的参考。

items.body: Dina Summer releases the synthpop single “Burning Heart” on 9 September 2026 via Iptamenos Discos. The track is part of the trio’s upcoming nine-track mini-album “Children Of The Night,” due 9 October 2026 on digital and vinyl. “Burning Heart” explores the pull of an imbalanced relationship, with the singer asking her partner to “cross the line” and return her affections. Sparkling organ synths sit against a propulsive dark bassline, pairing a nocturnal, club-ready sound with 1980s-style synthpop songwriting. Paris-based filmmaker Ceyda Yagiz directed the accompanying music video. “Children Of The Night” takes its title from Bela Lugosi’s line in the 1931 film “Dracula.” Iptamenos Discos will release the mini-album on black vinyl and on a blood red/black marbled vinyl edition, alongside the digital format. Dina Summer will tour behind the record, with festival dates including Wave Gotik Treffen, Amphi Festival, E-Tropolis Festival, Grauzone Festival, Out Of Line Weekender, Katzenclub Festival, Extramuralhas and Baroeg, plus headline shows in Berlin, London, Paris, Athens, Bogotá, São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Santiago and Buenos Aires. About Dina Summer Dina Summer is the Berlin-based collaborative project of Greek-German dark-disco duo Local Suicide and Bavarian electronic producer Kalipo, who began working together in 2019. The project draws on 1980s Italo disco, new wave, EBM and early-2000s electroclash for a dark, retro-futuristic synthpop sound. Dina Summer released the single “Schall & Rauch” in October 2024, then announced the mini-album “Children Of The Night” in June 2026. The trio followed with the singles “Bats in Paris” in July and “Rat Race” in August, and now “Burning Heart” arrives ahead of the mini-album’s 9 October release on Iptamenos Discos.

items.body: Breaking a person rarely begins with one spectacular act. More often, it is repetition that does the work: the same insult, the same reduction, the same pressure applied until endurance is mistaken for consent. Yet endurance can hold an unexpected force of its own. A flower may bend beneath the serpent, but the serpent still depends upon the flower to keep it from falling. Los Angeles shoegaze-punk band Taleen Kali enters that struggle with “Viper,” the lead single from its forthcoming second album, AEPEX, due in early 2027 through Dum Dum Records. Written as a palindrome, the song traps aggressor and victim inside a circular design of taking, breaking, and being driven down, while its central image turns apparent fragility into an instrument of survival. “Viper” opens upon a heavy, sustained guitar figure whose shoegaze distortion carries the physical weight of metal without sacrificing melody. Taleen Kali’s voice rises through the dense guitars with a majestic, almost otherworldly radiance, pulling the song toward the grand scale of ’90s alternative rock and psychedelic shoegaze. There is also an older pop instinct beneath the volume, particularly in the way the melody keeps climbing above the riff. Around the two-minute-and-forty-five-second mark, the arrangement changes course with an almost progressive-rock turn before closing inside one final rush of guitar noise. The band explains: “‘Viper’ is written in the form of a palindrome; it has this cyclical format that isn’t like any of our previous songs. I wanted to write a song about the fractured feminine, about what can happen when we try to break someone down over and over again and again. I remember seeing this nature video of a bright blue viper coiled and perched on top of a red rose, and the rose was holding up the entire weight of this thing–it wouldn’t bend or break. It was fascinating, so it became the artwork for the single and informed a lot of the visuals of our music video.” That circular structure appears directly in the lyrics, where “Viper / Take her / Viper / Break her” reverses and repeats like a command that has become impossible to escape. Against it stands the image of the wilted flower upon an altar: burdened, objectified, and repeatedly pushed downward, yet never quite destroyed. Directed by Alex LeGolvan, the accompanying video moves between a pale woodland, an enclosed red chamber, mirrored band performances, and the physical movements of dancer Lark Detweiler. Kali appears in white beneath the trees before the imagery descends into deeper reds and magentas, where flesh, leather, metal, mirrors, and guitar strings are filmed in close detail. The dancer’s body alternately strains, recoils, and reaches outward, giving human form to the song’s repeated acts of restraint and attempted escape. The video’s viper is no metaphorical stand-in. Nagel the snake, handled by animal wrangler Lyndsey Parker, glides across the body in the final sequence, making the song’s burden intimate and tangible. Taleen Kali, Miles Marsico, Genevieve Quiquivix, and Joseph D’Alfonso appear as the band reflected in mirrors, their performance partially concealed by glass, framing, and red light. Cinematographer Kai McNight gives the forest passages a bleached, exposed quality before the enclosed scenes turn warmer and more claustrophobic. The video was edited and colored by T.J. Maries-Hunt, with guitars provided by Fender. The flower may appear delicate, but it is the structure holding the predator aloft. Watch the video for “Viper” below: AEPEX marks a darker and heavier direction for Taleen Kali, drawing upon influences including The Horrors, Sextile, L.A. Witch, Tamaryn, Curve, and Chapterhouse. Across the record, breakbeat drums, abrupt rhythmic changes, Middle Eastern melodies, massed guitar fuzz, and Kali’s movement between commanding and sugar-sweet vocals carry the band beyond the romantic punk and beach-goth character of its earlier work and into more severe psychedelic terrain. The band returned to The Cave Studios to record with engineer and producer Josiah Mazzaschi, whose credits include Light FM, Bizou, and Child Seat. Mazzaschi also mixed and mastered the album, while Chris King of Cold Showers and Kai Tak contributed additional mixing to “Aepex” and “Crossed.” AFI’s Hunter Burgan plays saxophone on the dark psychedelic riot-grrrl track “Black Rose” and bass on “Eternal Eye.” AEPEX also marks Kali’s first time serving as co-producer on a full-length album, working alongside Miles Marsico and Mazzaschi. Guitarist Genevieve Quiquivix joins Kali and Mazzaschi across the record, with former guitarist Royce Hsu contributing several cameo solos. Ciara DeAlba, Marsico, and Mazzaschi provide backing vocals. Taleen Kali released the debut EP Soul Songs in 2018, followed by the Jeff Schroeder and Josiah Mazzaschi-produced debut album Flower of Life in 2023. The band later issued the remix collection Flower of Death in 2024, and the alternative love-song covers EP Covered in 2025. Its current lineup consists of Taleen Kali on vocals and guitar, Genevieve Quiquivix on guitar, Miles Marsico on bass, and Ciara DeAlba on drums. Taleen Kali celebrates the single with a headlining performance at Bar Sinister in Los Angeles on September 12. Listen to “Viper” below and purchase the single through Bandcamp. AEPEX arrives in early 2027 via Dum Dum Records. items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets
items.label: Hudson
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年曼彻斯特彼得卢屠杀为题材，Sean Cooney创作原创歌曲并联合Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter等多位英国民谣艺人，以多媒体书籍形式呈现历史叙事。专辑通过个人化的视角聚焦普通民众的故事，捕捉集会日的期待与恐惧、骑兵冲散的混乱以及事后的悲恸。音乐层面属于英式工业民谣传统，融合叙事性民谣与历史吟诵，乐器编制包括吉他、小提琴与各类质感乐器，演唱以情感充沛的人声为核心。整体定位偏向世界音乐范畴下的英伦传统民谣，但实验性与前卫元素有限，叙事结构传统扎实。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."

items._cn_summary: 这张作品并非传统意义上的音乐专辑，而是声音录音师伊恩·布伦南在芝加哥南区街头录制的口述实录。二十五名遭受枪支暴力影响的居民参与录音，年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，讲述范围涵盖施暴与受害两端。一位居高的母亲在讲述中失去两位儿子的经历时情感崩溃，反复道歉——而作者指出社会才是真正应该道歉的一方。录音地点位于一位九十四岁祖母家的前廊，正值特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队的当天。背景中混杂着环境噪音：迷德威机场飞机降落路径下的轰鸣、流浪狗的徘徊、院子里的蚊虫。没有添加任何音乐层。这是一次田野录音与社会纪实写作的结合，所有收益捐赠给以公共卫生方法遏制暴力的公益机构。

items.album: 【ARBAN WEEKLY／今週のニュースまとめ】コルトレーン生誕100年、サリヴァン・フォートナー、ステフォン・ハリスの新作など
items.excerpt: コルトレーン生誕100年—東洋への視線は誰に受け継がれたか 2026年9月1日、ジョン・コルトレーンの生誕100周年を記念する特集をNPRが組んだ。コルトレーンは1926年9月23日生まれで、今回の特集はその節目を前にした報道である。60年代半ば、コルトレーンは東洋音楽やスピリチュアルな思想への接近を深めていったとされる。単なる異文化への憧れではなく、サックスという楽器そのものを通じて瞑想的な音響空間を作ろうとした試みだったと言われている。 この視線は、彼の死後も途切れなかった。妻であり音楽家のアリス・コルトレーンは、インドの聖典やラーガの構造を自身の作品に取り込み、スピリチュアルジャズという系譜を独自に開拓した人物として知られる。同時代を並走したファラオ・サンダースも、アフリカと東洋の要素を重ねた音響を追求し続けた。近年ではカマシ・ワシントンが、大作を通じてこの系譜を現代のジャズ・オーケストレーションとして甦らせている。 生誕100年という数字そのものより、コルトレーンが開いた「サックスの向こう側」への扉が、半世紀以上経ってなお閉じていないことのほうが、記念すべき事実なのかもしれない
items.body: コルトレーン生誕100年—東洋への視線は誰に受け継がれたか 2026年9月1日、ジョン・コルトレーンの生誕100周年を記念する特集をNPRが組んだ。コルトレーンは1926年9月23日生まれで、今回の特集はその節目を前にした報道である。60年代半ば、コルトレーンは東洋音楽やスピリチュアルな思想への接近を深めていったとされる。単なる異文化への憧れではなく、サックスという楽器そのものを通じて瞑想的な音響空間を作ろうとした試みだったと言われている。 この視線は、彼の死後も途切れなかった。妻であり音楽家のアリス・コルトレーンは、インドの聖典やラーガの構造を自身の作品に取り込み、スピリチュアルジャズという系譜を独自に開拓した人物として知られる。同時代を並走したファラオ・サンダースも、アフリカと東洋の要素を重ねた音響を追求し続けた。近年ではカマシ・ワシントンが、大作を通じてこの系譜を現代のジャズ・オーケストレーションとして甦らせている。 生誕100年という数字そのものより、コルトレーンが開いた「サックスの向こう側」への扉が、半世紀以上経ってなお閉じていないことのほうが、記念すべき事実なのかもしれない。 出典：https://www.npr.org/2026/09/01/nx-s1-5951499/celebrating-100-years-of-jazz-great-john-coltrane ロン・カーター×ヨタム・シルバースタイン、ピアノレス・デュオの系譜 ジャズ専門誌『Jazz Journal』が8-9月の新譜ガイドを発表した。中でも注目したいのが、ベーシスト、ロン・カーターとギタリスト、ヨタム・シルバースタインによるデュエット作である。これはジム・ホールへのトリビュートとして企画されたという。   ロン・カーターとジム・ホールは、かつてベースとギターだけで対話する録音を残している。伴奏を必要としないピアノレス・デュオという形式は、当時としては実験的な試みだった。今回のシルバースタインとの再演は、その系譜を半世紀後の若い世代の手に橋渡しする作業とも言える。 なお同時期には、Sidiki Camaraの野心作、Tristan Cappelの追悼盤、15年ぶりとなるDeirdre Cartwrightの新作も発表されている。それぞれの詳細は今後の紹介に譲りたい。 出典：https://jazzjournal.co.uk/2026/08/30/new-releases-august-september-2026-c-d サリヴァン・フォートナー、ニューオーリンズの記憶を刻む ニューオーリンズ出身のピアニスト、サリヴァン・フォートナーが新作『Leave That In There』を発表した。ベーシストのタイロン・アレン2世、ドラマーのカイボン・ゴードンとの常編成トリオによる初のスタジオ録音である。 アルバム名は、ハリケーン・カトリーナを記録したドキュメンタリー映画『When the Levees Broke』（スパイク・リー監督、2006年）の台詞から取られたという。収録される12曲のオリジナルと再演には、ルイジアナ南部の風景や家族の記憶、黒人ディアスポラの伝統が織り込まれているとのことだ。 堤防が決壊し、街が水に沈んだあの記憶を、20年近くを経て一枚の音楽作品として刻み直す——グラミー受賞歴のあるピアニストによる、極めて個人的でありながら土地の歴史そのものでもある企画である。 出典：https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/sullivan-fortner-trio-apres-le-deluge-espoir-et-resilience-2428000 rd ウェンデル・ハリソンが語る、ファラオ・サンダースとサン・ラーの記憶 デトロイトのジャズ・アヴァンギャルドシーンを長く支えてきたウェンデル・ハリソンが、ele-kingのインタビューでファラオ・サンダースとサン・ラーとの出会いを振り返っている。デトロイトは、モータウンのサウンドで語られることが多い都市だが、同時にジャズの実験精神が根を張った土地でもあった。ハリソン自身、クラリネット奏者・サックス奏者としてこの街のシーン形成に長く携わってきた当事者であり、その証言には固有の重みがある。 インタビューでハリソンは、サンダースの音の探求とサン・ラーの宇宙的な音楽哲学、二人の巨人がそれぞれ異なる方向からスピリチュアル・ジャズの地平を切り開いていった様子を語る。一人の証人が二つの潮流を同時に見ていたという事実は、ジャズ史を線ではなく面として捉え直す手がかりになる。デトロイトという土地が、ニューヨークとは異なる形でアヴァンギャルドの拠点になり得たことも、この証言を通じて浮かび上がってくる。 出典：https://www.ele-king.net/interviews/012378 Stefon Harris & Blackout、20年の歩みと友への追悼 ヴィブラフォン奏者、ステフォン・ハリスが率いるBlackoutが、結成20周年を記念したアルバム『Legacy Dances』をMotémaからリリースした。本作は単なる周年企画ではなく、バンドの創設メンバーだったケイシー・ベンジャミンへの追悼という側面を色濃く持つ。 Blackoutは電子的な音響処理とアコースティックな演奏を融合させ、ジャズの語法を拡張してきたバンドである。本作ではルイ・アームストロング、ウィリー・ザ・ライオン・スミス、そして詩人アミリ・バラカへのオマージュも織り込まれ、ジャズを「共感の行動」として捉え直す哲学的な仕上がりになっているという。20年という時間の蓄積と、そこに刻まれた喪失が、一枚のアルバムのなかで響き合っている。 出典： https://www.radiofrance.fr/francemusique/podcasts/au-coeur-du-jazz/stefon-harris-blackout-feat-casey-benjamin-hommage-et-compagnonage-7477111 投稿 【ARBAN WEEKLY／今週のニュースまとめ】コルトレーン生誕100年、サリヴァン・フォートナー、ステフォン・ハリスの新作など は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items._cn_summary: Steve Lacy 暌违四年推出的新作，横跨多种风格边界。从吉他主导的另类摇滚与梦幻流行，到与 Erykah Badu 合作的三拍子慢速嘻哈段落，专辑呈现出广阔的音乐光谱。评论指出这种广角式的手法映射了艺术家人生中的混沌状态，作品还融合了 SZA 与 Cecil Blevins 的元素。整体延续了前作大热单曲'Bad Habit'所建立的吉他英雄形象，但在风格跨度上更为大胆，试图突破单一标签的局限。The Internet 重组在即，这张作品也可视为其个人探索阶段的阶段性总结。

items.body: 目次 〈誰もが思っているけど、わざわざ口にしないこと〉を口にする AIで生成された曲は応援する相手がいない “Analog Intelligence”は僕自身の決意の歌 asmiと成長した新入社員の平日を歌った“週末のマーチ (Weekday Version)” 人に直接会って自分の音楽をぶつけたい ツインギターが幾何学的に絡み合い、目まぐるしく展開するアンサンブルの上を、スリリングかつ高揚感あふれるメロディーが駆け抜けていく。吉國唯をゲストボーカルに迎え配信リリースされたRyo Umekawaの新曲“Analog Intelligence”は、高密度でスリリングなポストロック／オルタナティブロックであると同時に、AI時代に人間が音楽を作る意味を問いかける一曲だ。 一方、asmiと歌う“週末のマーチ (Weekday Version)”では、ブラスを交えたカラフルなサウンドとコミカルな掛け合いによって、働く日々の慌ただしさをポップに描き出す。こちらは2026年9月30日（水）にタワーレコード限定で CDシングル としてリリースされる。 一見対照的な2作だが、そこには〈誰もが抱えながら、わざわざ口にしないことを歌う〉というRyo Umekawaの姿勢が一貫している。 会社員として働きながら、週末を中心に作曲、作詞、編曲、録音を行ってきたRyo Umekawa。ほぼ初めてとなるロングインタビューで、その歩みと制作方法、AI音楽に対する率直な感情、そして人と人をつなぐものとしての音楽について聞いた。 〈誰もが思っているけど、わざわざ口にしないこと〉を口にする ――音楽を始めたきっかけから教えてください。 「中学2年生の頃、母親が姉にギターを買ってきたんです。でも、姉は2日くらいでやめてしまって（笑）。そのまま置いてあったギターを僕が触るようになり、ようやく1曲弾き語りができたところから、本格的に音楽を聴くようになりました。最初によく聴いていたのはスピッツや斉藤和義さんなど、フォークソング寄りの音楽です」 ――その後、かなり早い段階から曲作りや録音も始めたそうですね。 「中学3年生くらいでバンドを始めました。人に見せるには音源があった方がいいけれど、当時は誰かに録音してもらえる環境もなかった。それで家のパソコンにソフトを入れて、ある程度聴ける形にできないか研究し始めたんです。バンドではオリジナル曲を中心に活動して、僕が作曲することが多かったですね」 ――吉國唯さんとのユニット〈カシコ、阻上ノ鯉〉は、どのように始まったのでしょう? 「最初にやっていたロックバンドが解散した頃には、DTMのスキルも少しずつ身についていました。僕らは北海道出身なんですけど、当時、札幌で別のバンドにいた吉國さんの歌がすごく良くて、自分の曲を歌ってもらえたら面白いだろうと思って声をかけたんです。対バンなどを通じて知り合っていて、仲も良かったので、〈いいよ、やろうよ〉と言ってくれました」
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章采访了一位兼职业余音乐人Ryo Umekawa，介绍了他两首新作品。一首是与吉國唯合作的“Analog Intelligence”，被描述为高密度、刺激的后摇滚与另类摇滚结合，探讨AI时代人类创作音乐的意义；另一首是与asmi合作的“週末のマーチ（Weekday Version）”，以铜管乐和幽默对唱呈现上班族日常的忙碌感。文中还回顾了他从中学时代开始接触吉他、自学DTM录音、组建乐队并与札幌音乐人合作的经历。文章侧重人物访谈和创作理念阐述，对音乐本身的制作细节和声音设计讨论有限，整体偏向主流独立摇滚和流行摇滚范畴。

items._cn_summary: 长笛演奏家克莱尔·蔡斯发起了名为"Density 2036"的长期协作项目，旨在重新思考当代音乐中作曲者与演奏者之间僵化的角色分工。该项目从体制层面出发，挑战现有的资助体系——如资助金、巡演和驻留项目——对音乐家创作方式的限制。蔡斯认为，这种依附于既有体系的创作模式在解决部分问题的同时，也制造了新的创作困境。项目周期跨度至2036年，强调音乐家之间的深度协作，并试图构建一种更灵活、更具实验性的当代古典音乐实践模式。这一项目体现了表演者主动介入策展与创作过程的趋势，对学院体制提出了实质性的反思。

Schmidt 则与 Obel Feldi 合作呈现另一场特别演出。原定登台的 JG Thirlwell 将以 Foetus 名义携二十人室内乐团完成压轴。文中提及的艺术家多活跃于实验与前卫音乐领域，但文章本身为资讯性质，缺少音乐评论内容，仅作为演出信息播报。

items.body: At 79 years old, the former Yellow Magic Orchestra and Happy End member has produced a true labour of love, offering a sometimes croonsome window on the sunlit uplands Photo credit: Masahiro Handa ‘Sincerity’ isn’t quite the word that springs to mind when considering Haruomi Hosono’s fifty years worth of solo albums. Not only were Hosono’s two famous pop groups – the Japanese-language folk-rock quartet Happy End, and the wildly innovative technopop trio Yellow Magic Orchestra – consummate ironists, his couple of dozen solo albums, hopping impatiently from style to style, from decade to decade, were never confessional or intimate or emotionally driven. Rather, they were music about music, pop about pop, with a subject matter that was more likely to revolve... The post The Beautiful World: Yours Sincerely by Haruomi Hosono appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这是细野晴臣在七十九岁高龄推出的个人专辑，被乐评形容为一段充满个人情感的作品。细野晴臣曾是日本传奇乐队Happy End（民谣摇滚）和Yellow Magic Orchestra（电子流行）的核心成员，后者以创新性的电子合成器运用闻名于世。乐评指出，他此前的大量个人专辑以风格跳跃著称，从不拘泥于单一类型，更倾向于关于音乐的音乐、元音乐式的解构方式。这篇文章内容较短，大量正文被截断，只能看到引言部分和乐评的基本框架。文章来自The Quietus，属于独立音乐媒体，但内容深度和细节因截断而受限。整体而言，专辑融合了细野晴臣职业生涯的多种影响，从早期民谣到电子实验，但具体这张专辑的创新点和音乐特征因内容截断而无法深入了解。

items.body: Review by yarstruly — Copied from my review at my blog, "Scott's Song by Song Spotlights", where there are links for listening and purchasing.Clicking 5, but really 4.75, nearly perfect, but not quite!The artists on today's album require no introduction for most people who will be reading this. Steve Hackett & Steve Rothery have come together to create an album of instrumental music. Of course, most of you know that Steve Hackett is best known as the lead guitarist in Genesis from 1971-1977, and has had a prolific solo career since 1975, also collaborating with Steve Howe in 1986 in GTR and Chris Squire in "Squackett" in 2011-12. Steve Rothery has been the lead guitarist of Marillion on every album in their catalog plus his solo album "Ghosts of Pripyat" in 2014. Both guitarists are highly respected for their guitar skills and compositional abilities. This album is a decade in the making, with the two coming together when they could at each of their home studios and a studio called The Racket Club. The theme of the album is "the elemental power of the sea". Finally on August 28, 2026, "The Roaring Waves" will be released on InsideOut Records. Rounding out the recordings are:- Steve Hackett / guitar, harmonica- Steve Rothery / guitar, bass, keyboards- Riccardo Romano / keyboards, bass- Daniele Pomo / drums (1-5)- Leon Parr / drums (6,7)I want to thank Oliver Bergmann from Oktober Promotions, and Sharon Chevin for directing me to Oliver. As always, I receive no further compensation, and I call it like I hear it. As per my usual method, this is a cold listen.Time to check out the music!Track 1 - The Storm (6:50)The track fades in with ocean sounds, then a mellotron string part takes over. A lead guitar melody begins, and a bolero type of rhythm begins to emerge. At 2:17 there is the sound of thunder, and a guitar riff takes the spotlight. The drums and bass are tight. This is ominous, of course, as the track depicts a storm out at sea. The guitar solo at 3:40 sounds like Rothery to my ears, but I have no indication of who is playing what. I believe Hackett took over at around 4:25; but then again, I could be wrong. The guitarists then alternate licks. This is wonderful! At around 6:00 the storm seems to come to an end and things resolve peacefully. Awesome opener!Track 2 - Sandsend (4:46)After a note that fades in, there is a calm moderate tempoed rhythm with the guitarists alternating phrases on the melody. We are in calmer, gently rocking seas now. The synth gets the spotlight briefly at 1:50. This is a nice chill-out piece of music from these guitar masters. In the last minute or so of the track, however. The musical tension seems to build up a bit. Still, it stays pretty calm. Nice track!Track 3 - Red Dragon (4:19)This has a droning, bagpipe-like quality in the intro. When the rhythm section comes in, the tempo is slightly more upbeat. I like the use of controlled feedback. One of the players has a sitar-like tone on the arpeggiated tones. I like the soundscape on this. The tempo double-times at around 2 minutes, briefly. There are a wealth of interesting tones being utilized. The focus is on the music, not the players' virtuosic abilities. Well done; an enjoyable track!Track 4 - The Roaring Waves (7:11)The title track is up next, and the name promises an exciting ride! Hackett (I assume) starts out with an impressive classical guitar bit. An ominous crescendo takes us to an orchestrated keyboard part that establishes the backdrop for the lead guitar. Not sure which one plays what, but I bet it was Steve. Obviously, both players have built a fine reputation for their abilities. The arrangement on this one is more involved than in the previous tracks. I love the crescendo at around 5:00. I like how the two are playing countermelodies at around 5:30. The classical guitar returns to close out this wonderful dynamic track. This one is my favorite, thus far. Track 5 - K-129 (7:52) According to the notes I was provided:Cinematic is right. Songs like the claustrophobic K-129, which details a submarine's final voyage to the bottom of the seabed, dark waters swirling up around it as its crew meet their doom. "You're trying to create an atmosphere", says Rothery. "I came up with the original sequenced sound, and then it's like painting a picture. You have the rhythmical and the melodic and atmospheric elements that you try and construct in such a way to take people on a journey. And it's a fascinating story. Conspiracy theorists think this Russian submarine that went missing at the end of the 60s was trying to start a war between the States and China and that the captain scuttled the ship rather than let them start World War III, incredible."The aforementioned sequence commences the track. Atmospheric guitar tones and occasional drums are peppered over the top. This one is a slow burn. Of course, there are some sonar sound effects along the way to evoke the atmosphere of a submarine. At around 4:14 a steady drum groove begins. The guitarists' lead-lines break some of the musical tension. The rhythm stops before 5:30. A new beat returns just after 6 minutes. The guitar parts are glorious! The track concludes with a single sonar tone. Terrific track. Track 6 - The Black Sea (6:41)According to the notes provided, the (actual) Black Sea is littered with the skeletons of more than 1,000 shipwrecks over the centuries. That will certainly inform the tone of this piece. It begins with a sense of foreboding. There are wonderful clean guitar tones intertwining in the first segment over a gentle 6-8 meter. A melody takes over at around 1:45. The tone of this track is very warm and melodic. There is a sense of forward motion throughout. The two play together at around 5:00 as the music reaches its climax. Afterwards, there is a peaceful resolution. File this under hauntingly beautiful. I love it!Track 7 - Pacific Coast Highway (7:31)Hackett kicks this one off with a bluesy harmonica riff that would make Huey Lewis smile. This one is a fun driving tune! There are even some wordless backing vocals. Hackett's harmonica playing is a noteworthy feature of this track, as Rothery quipped in the info sheet:"And Steve's harmonica on that is so, so good. He said to me at one point, you know, sometimes I think I should have been a harmonica player instead of (a) guitar player."There is still plenty of great guitar playing to be had, though. This one even reminds me, stylistically, of a Joe Satriani tune. This is the one where they cut loose and have some fun! And we as listeners reap the benefits! I like the syncopated riff starting around 5:15. They finally let some shredding licks loose at around 6:10. The final minute of the song has glorious choral music "aahhs". Great ending to a great album.OVERALL IMPRESSIONS:I loved it! However, don't expect a proggy flurry of odd-meters and flashy solos. No, this is about the music and creating sound pictures in a cinematic way. The compositions and arrangements are top notch. The production is immaculate. If you are looking for an immersive musical experience, this is the album for you! Of course, it's fun to try to pick out which guitarist is playing what line, it's probably better to forget all of that, and let the music wash over you. I'm giving this a 4.75 out of 5 stars (95%).
items._cn_summary: 这是Steve Hackett与Steve Rothery两位吉他手的合作器乐专辑，主题围绕海洋元素力量展开，历经多次录音室合作后于2026年由InsideOut厂牌发行。两位吉他手分别贡献吉他与和声、贝斯与键盘演奏，另有键盘、鼓手配合完成七首曲目。从已听三首来看，作品以mellotron弦乐铺底、吉他旋律线交替为核心手法，融入了波浪采样、雷声等环境声效，部分段落运用受控反馈与西塔琴般的音色处理。整体呈现出渐进摇滚框架内的器乐对话，氛围从风暴的压迫感过渡到海湾的宁静。乐评详细记录了每分钟的音乐变化，但作品整体仍属传统前卫摇滚范畴，与实验、前卫或即兴类口味的交集有限。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the earliest Krautrock bands actually began as early as 1964 as the beat group Bentox whichwas founded by the Swiss B�eler twins, Thomas Leidenberger, and Lucky Schmidt and found themselvestouring both Asia and Germany alike however to little financial gain. By 1971 the act grew to aquintet and jumped on the burgeoning psychedelic rock scene known as Krautrock which was takingGermany by storm. With Krautrock you never really know what you're gonna get as sometimes it'sfreaky and folky and other times loud and raucous. As the newly renamed WIND, the band set sail intothe world of psychedelia adopting a plethora of sounds that included not only the kosmische soundsthat were propelled by the likes of Amon Duul II and Guru Guru but the band also looked towards theUK for inspiration drawing some of the heavy psych / early metal moments heard by the likes of UriahHeep and Deep Purple. The band's debut SEASONS showcased these styles set to a heavy psychedelic setting with not only acompetent vocalist but an organ-drenched freakout style of heavier rock with dramatic guitardistortion, fast tempos and even a drummer to keep up with it all. As much proto-metal as lysergic60s psych, WIND also focused on dreamy folk fueled passages and classical excursions making SEASONSa nice varied heady mix into a instrumentally competency seasoned with the psychedelically detached.This band from Erlangen near Nuremberg was apparently seeking a more international acceptance withlyrics in English and nice catchy melodic hooks that kept one foot in the accessible rock paradigmall the while adding the final touches of the more psychedelic Krautrock attributes that the mostadventurous trippers were dishing out in full abundance. The album features six tracks that add up to nearly 42 minutes with the final closing "RedMorningbird" just missing the 16-minute mark. While many tracks are clearly on the heavier sideincluding the opening powerhouse "What We Do Now" and the heavy as a ton of bricks "Dear LittleFriend," other tracks such as "Now It's Over" and "Romance" are more subdued and laced with soaringflute runs and acoustic guitar, touches of jazz and a completely different vibe than the heavierside of the album. The lengthy closer is perhaps the most koschmische expansive progressive piece onthe album with long instrumental drifting, dreaming meditative soundscapes and ethereal nonchalancethrough planet Lysergia although the track eventually bursts into the heavier rock. While many mayfind this album disjointed in its wild mood swings from heavy rockers on acid to well, just plainblitzed out on acid, the ease of how this cast of characters adapts from one extreme to another isactually quite brilliant and for my tastes it all offers a nice varying palette of mood settings.Sounding like Uriah Heep or Deep Purple from a parallel universe, WIND managed to emulate other actsbut really sounds fairly unique in its little in-between zone where heavy psych meets the mosttrippy expansive mediative side of Krautrock. It's actually the perfect album for 1971 which stillshowcased prog as unfinished business that hadn't quite found those formulaic approaches. WINDsuccessfully captured the heavy organ rock aspects that were en vogue at the time as well ascapturing the essence of a true psychedelic Kraut band. Perhaps the closest band i've heard toWIND's first album is another German band, Twenty Sixty Six And Then which released it's classic oneoff the very next year. Overall this is quality progressive heavy psych from 1971 Germany. The banddid release one following album but shed the rock aspects and went full on folk, a move that provedto be the band's undoing but perhaps the comparisons to Uriah Heep were too much and even thoughthis album does remind a lot of that band's earliest prog releases, it's still distinct enough standon its own two feet.
items._genre: krautrock / psychedelic rock / hard rock / proto-metal
items._cn_summary: WIND乐队的首张专辑《Seasons》融合了德国Krautrock运动中典型的迷幻摇滚元素，涵盖从重型的硬摇滚、proto-metal到梦幻民谣、爵士律动以及长达近16分钟的宇宙飘移式器乐段落。乐队在重型迷幻与柔和原声之间频繁切换，展现出对Uriah Heep和Deep Purple等英国乐队的致敬，同时融入Amon Düül II式的Kosmische氛围。键盘主导的迷幻暴走、吉他失真、快速的节奏与长笛、民谣吉他段落交替出现，形成丰富但略显凌乱的整体情绪图谱。对于偏好实验前卫、学院派爵士与电子融合的听众而言，这张作品虽有一定的跨领域尝试，但本质上仍属1970年代早期摇滚框架内的类型作品，与深度实验路线的距离较大。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — It was a strange era, a time of change and readjustment, and one where it was easy to lose one's way. Musicians who wished to stay the course had to confront record labels and even critics who accused them of self-plagiarism; yet, on the other hand, changing direction was seen as an act of betrayal. Nevertheless, Jon Anderson transitioned from making his recording debut as a solo artist to surrounding himself with friends for his second album, Song of Seven, a number that held deep significance for him, symbolizing both the inner quest and a sense of wholeness.The lineup included Dick Morrissey, saxophonist for the jazz-fusion band If; bassist John Giblin (formerly of Brand X); and Morris Pert on drums and percussion, along with, of course, Jack Bruce and Simon Phillips. With this dynamic, groove-laden band, plus additional musicians and a string quartet, Jon handled acoustic guitar, keyboards, and the harp. He composed songs that, while initially striking due to their ultra-modern, early-80s production style (as heard on "For You for Me"), ultimately reveal themselves to be classic Anderson tracks: deeply emotional and reminiscent of his collaborations with Vangelis. It is an epic sound; backed by such solid musicians, the music creates a rich sonic tapestry that colors the scene much like the stained-glass artwork on the album cover. "Some Are Born" is a beautiful acoustic song that could easily have fit into the Yes repertoire had he been recording with his bandmates.There are symphonic touches alongside rhythms that were more contemporary for that era, such as soul, funk, and a bit of jazz (though not the most daring kind). There is something ethnic about "Don't Forget (Nostalgia), something Latin, that is enhanced by John Dankworth's saxophone; meanwhile, "Heart of the Matter," despite its more pop-rock format, is filled with Jon's signature positive energy, and the rhythm section of Jack Bruce on bass and Simon Phillips on drums provides excellent support for the track."Hear It" is a beautiful track, one could easily imagine it within the context of Yes, yet it stands on its own; it embodies Jon's spirit, which possesses a distinct identity of its own, always positive and visionary, inviting the listener to share in that outlook. "Everybody Loves You" has a rhythm that always reminded me of the songs Carole King and Gerry Goffin used to write; I could even picture it on Tapestry. The bass work, along with Morris Pert's percussion, lends the track a warm, jazzy feel, while the arrangement retains a certain complexity toward the end."Take Your Time" is almost a beautiful waltz, enhanced by Giblin's fretless bass and unmistakably Anderson-esque. By the time "Days" arrives, the album has transcended any specific era to become timeless; it features Jon, his guitar, and his signature magic, with minimal keyboard and bass accompaniment, just enough to let the music of his words cast the spell."Song of Seven" is, logically, the title track, and for me, it acts as a counterweight to the rest of the 'lbum, working not in isolation, but as part of the whole. The strings usher in a different atmosphere, one that is more sacred, and mark the point of greatest resemblance to Yes; indeed, at times it is hard to distinguish it from that band, given Jon's unmistakable voice. Rich in melody and character, the song stands tall on its own merits, earning a place among the very best in his repertoire, akin in spirit to the Going for the One era of Yes.A solid album that fits perfectly into the discography and perfectly explains the subsequent trajectory, including further adventures with Vangelis on Short Stories (1980) and Animation (1982), thereby rounding out that concept of wholeness.
items._cn_summary: Jon Anderson离开Yes乐队后录制的第二张个人专辑，以弦乐四重奏和爵士乐手阵容为基础，呈现出八十年代初的制作风格。整张专辑融合了灵魂、芬克、爵士与拉丁元素，搭配Anderson标志性的高音假声与乐观情绪的人声旋律。虽然歌词与编曲仍带有Yes时期的史诗感和精神探索主题，但整体方向更偏向融合流行，而非前卫摇滚的实验性边缘。Jack Bruce的低音线与Simon Phillips的鼓点提供了稳定的节奏骨架，部分曲目接近Carole King式的温暖流行质感。专辑试图在商业可听性与艺术完整性之间取得平衡，结果是一张制作精良但缺少突破性聆听体验的作品。

items.body: Dismantled are back with new material. Gary Zon‘s electro-industrial project will release the new single “Zero” on 18 September 2026 through Metropolis Records, with a new full-length album set to follow in November. The six-minute track is already listed by digital retailers as a Metropolis release, while the label’s current Dismantled page continues to carry the project’s catalogue. There is considerably more history behind “Zero” than the announcement might initially suggest. The track first surfaced as part of a three-song preview for an album called “Endless”, uploaded to Dismantled’s Bandcamp in November 2021 alongside previews of “Mirror’s Edge” and “Poison”. At the time, the album was expected in 2022 through Metropolis Records in North America and Dependent Records in Europe. The project itself had been announced even earlier. In May 2020, Zon revealed through Metropolis that he was working on an album titled “Endless”, which he described at the time as combining different periods of the Dismantled catalogue into a more cohesive sound, specifically referencing Standard Issue, the self-titled debut and The War Inside Me. That announcement accompanied “No Escape”, a track written during the early months of the pandemic. Six years later, a current retail listing gives “Endless” a 20 November 2026 release date on CD, with the catalogue number/EAN 0782388148320. Metropolis has not yet published a complete 2026 album page, tracklist or detailed production credits, so those details remain unconfirmed for now. “Zero” therefore functions both as the beginning of Dismantled’s new release cycle and as the return of material that has been evolving publicly for several years. The single is listed at 6:14 and will be available digitally in 24-bit/44.1 kHz resolution. Beatport currently categorises the track under Ambient / Experimental and lists it at 110 BPM, although Dismantled’s own history has always been rooted much more broadly in electro-industrial, EBM and electronic music. About Dismantled Dismantled began as a studio experiment by Gary Zon in late 2000, initially inspired by the sound of Front Line Assembly. Zon gradually added vocals and drew on influences from film, television and electronic music, developing a layered combination of electro-industrial electronics, melody and trance elements. A first demo appeared through mp3.com in 2001; Dependent Records subsequently included “Purity” on its Septic II compilation, and Metropolis Records contacted Zon later that year. The self-titled debut followed through Metropolis in 2002, with Post Nuclear arriving in 2004. Later releases included the Breed To Death EP, Standard Issue, The War Inside Me in 2011, the Whole Wide World EP in 2012 and The Hero in 2016. Metropolis currently lists “No Escape” from 2020 as Dismantled’s most recent release in its catalogue. “Zero” marks the project’s first new material in six years. For now, what is confirmed is simple: “Zero” arrives on 18 September via Metropolis Records, and a new Dismantled album follows in November. All available evidence points toward that album being the long-developed Endless, but complete official album details from Metropolis are still awaited.
items._cn_summary: 本文以新闻报道形式介绍了Dismantled新单曲"Zero"及酝酿已久的专辑"Endless"的发行动态。项目主理人Gary Zon早在2020年便宣布制作这张专辑，试图融合其早期作品中标准发行版、自命名首专和《The War Inside Me》三个时期的声音，形成更统一的表达。新单曲时长六分钟，以24-bit/44.1kHz高解析度数字发行，Beatport将其归类为氛围/实验类，但项目本身始终植根于electro-industrial、EBM和电子音乐领域。文章追溯了Dismantled从2000年受Front Line Assembly启发起步，到2026年新专辑发行的完整历程，整体属于信息性新闻稿而非深入乐评，缺乏对音乐本身的实质性分析与评价。
