items.body: British violist, singer and composer Sophie Sirota released the remix album “Pressure Drop Remixed” on 10 September 2026 through Coastal Electronauts, the Whitstable, Kent collective on which she is a co-organiser alongside Martin Glover‘s associate Peter Coyte. The ten-track set reworks Sirota’s 2025 debut “Pressure Drop” through contributions from Youth (Killing Joke bassist and producer Martin Glover, who supplies two remixes), 4hero, Coyte’s own Shape Navigator alias, 3Head/Al Mac, Will Materialise, smelliott, BorjeNotBorje, Grace Griffin Blustery Day and Riigs. The release-day single “If I Wrote A Song Would You Like It? (Shape Navigator Remix)” carries a new video edit by @diz_qo, the visual artist who works regularly with Coastal Electronauts. Of the clip, @diz_qo said: “I was seeking inspiration for it and found an old photo I’d taken years ago of what I believe to be some kind of radar equipment. It somehow resonated with the track – its sense of transmitting and receiving, of searching for a signal – and became the starting point for its visual language.” Two other tracks from the album preceded it as singles, each with its own @diz_qo video edit: Youth’s nine-minute rework of “50:50 Pure Trance”, which Side-Line covered on its own release, and “mood (4hero remix)”, whose video arrived the same month. Coyte mixed and mastered the original “Pressure Drop” album, which made his contribution to the remix set direct. Sirota commented: “Peter has given me considerable support and encouragement during my solo journey, and we have collaborated on several live projects. He also mixed and mastered the original ‘Pressure Drop’ album, so asking him to remix something from it was inevitable. The result is this beautiful track.” On the remix project as a whole, Sirota said she gave contributors free rein: “I’ve been fortunate to work with some incredible musicians during my career and it has been humbling to receive so many positive reactions to the idea of making it. What each contributor has sent back has resulted in a really eclectic variety of styles and sounds. I left each remix to their discretion and deliberately gave no direction or input.” She also pointed to newer names on the tracklist: “I’m particularly pleased to have had a number of younger artists provide unique interpretations of my tracks, including people I have met through the vibrant EMOM scene. After all, this is what gave me the initial encouragement and support to create the original album.” The full “Pressure Drop Remixed” tracklist runs: “50:50 Pure Trance – The Endless Carousel of Lust and Suffering Dub (Youth remix)”, “mood (4hero remix)”, “if i wrote a song would you like it? (Shape Navigator remix)”, “sophie’s tension (3Head/Al Mac remix)”, “i feel (Will Materialise remix)”, “holding te (smelliott remix)”, “i feel (BorjeNotBorje remix)”, “if i wrote a song would you like it? (Grace Griffin Blustery Day remix)”, “holding tension (Riigs remix)” and a second Youth reading, “50:50 Pure Ambient – The Savage Orient of the Heart Dub”. The album streams on Spotify, Apple Music and Amazon Music, and is available as a digital download on Bandcamp. Pressure Drop Remixed by Sophie Sirota About Sophie Sirota Sophie Sirota is a classically trained violist, singer and composer who began working as a session violist while at music college, going on to work as a session player, live performer, arranger and composer with Paul Weller, Kim Deal, Tindersticks, Beth Orton, Ed Harcourt, 4hero, D’Influence, Gabrielle and Robert Kirby; her Discogs profile lists close to 100 credits and a place in the Wrecking Crew Quartet. She has lived in Whitstable, Kent for more than two decades. In early 2023 she started performing solo material, built from electric viola, effects pedals and voice, at the monthly Coastal Electronauts electronic-music sessions in Whitstable, which she now helps organise. That work led to her debut album “Pressure Drop”, released on 24 October 2025 through Coastal Electronauts on digital, CD and a 100-copy vinyl edition, mixed and mastered by Peter Coyte. Record Collector called the album “a fine example of innovative artistic imagination”. “Pressure Drop Remixed”, out 10 September 2026, extends that debut into collaborative territory, opening Sirota’s viola-based material to Youth, 4hero, Coyte’s Shape Navigator project and a wider group of electronic producers. No dedicated Wikipedia page for Sirota could be found at the time of writing.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是英国中提琴家Sophie Sirota首张专辑《Pressure Drop》的混音版本，集合了十位不同艺术家的重新诠释，包括Killing Joke贝斯手Youth（提供两首混音）、4hero、Shape Navigator、3Head/Al Mac等。Sirota完全放手让每位混音者自行创作，未提供任何方向或建议，呈现出风格颇为多元的混音集合。合作阵容来自Coastal Electronauts集体，该集体位于肯特郡惠特斯特布尔，是独立电子音乐厂牌。混音风格涵盖dub、trance、ambient等方向，与Sirota的中提琴演奏及电子实验美学形成对话。视觉部分由@diz_qo负责，部分单曲配有影像版本。文章整体偏向新闻发布性质，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评论与审美分析，信息量以事实陈述为主。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John于1999年在德国洛勒莱露天剧场的演出，由WDR旗下长期运行的音乐节目Rockpalast录制发行。演出以新奥尔良传统为底色，曲目涵盖'Iko Iko''Qualified''I Walk on Guilded Splinters'等经典，融合Mardi Gras游行音乐、funk、布鲁斯与爵士元素。伴奏乐队由吉他手Bobby Broom、贝斯David Barard与鼓手Herman Ernest组成，呈现紧凑而充满权威感的节奏框架。Dr. John在表演中展现其作为钢琴家与歌手的多面性，既处理经典新奥尔良曲目，也翻唱Duke Ellington的'I'm Gonna Go Fishin''，以Earl King的'Big Chief'收尾。从内容来看，这是一场对Dr. John既有曲目的高水准现场重现，侧重于地方音乐传统的舞台呈现，而非声音或结构上的实验探索。

items.body: Light percussion opens “Down Home”, the new single from Melbourne instrumental funk quartet Karate Boogaloo, before a bass line takes the lead at an easy mid-tempo. The drums lock into a hard, tight pocket on a kit that sounds close to falling apart, while organ and choppy guitar come in over the top. That rattling kit gives the rough edge to a tune named after anything simple and worn in. The main theme leans openly on nostalgia, and the band reckon anyone who has declared the riff dead should “check their specs“. Drummer Hudson Whitlock plays alongside Henry Jenkins on bass, Callum Riley on organ and Darvid Thor on guitar. The four met as classmates at a Melbourne high school and have played together for almost two decades. In our July interview with the band, Jenkins explained that Karate Boogaloo began strictly as a covers act devoted to The Meters and Booker T. & The MG’s. The change came with an original called “Stay Healthy”, which he described as the moment the band “crossed the River Rubicon“. “Down Home” precedes Access All Areas, due on 9 October through Colemine Records and College of Knowledge Records. In February 2027 Karate Boogaloo tour the UK, France and the Netherlands. The run opens on 3 February aboard V11, a 1951 British lightship docked in Rotterdam, and closes upstairs at Paradiso in Amsterdam on the 13th. The London date is at the Jazz Cafe on 5 February. Further nights follow at Hyde Park Book Club in Leeds, The Abbey in Manchester, The Jam Jar in Bristol, Le Tetris in Le Havre and POPUP! in Paris. Stream “Down Home” and order Access All Areas HERE   The post Daily Discovery: Karate Boogaloo – Down Home appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: Australian dark electro duo Avarice In Audio released “Welcome To Weimar America” on 11 September 2026 through Alfa Matrix. The 12-track digital album is the seventh full-length from Gerry Hawkins and Lawrie B (Studio-X) and pushes the duo’s sound toward industrial rock, elektro-metal and guitar-driven material. The tracklist runs “Welcome Home”, “Let Them Eat Violence”, “I Know You”, “Time To Swing”, “Bareback In Babylon”, “The End Is Nigh”, “Let The Boreal Burn (v.2026)” featuring Static Logic, “Prophet & Loss”, “Our Trade Is War”, “The Devil Gets His Due”, “Baroque Ruins” and an Avarice In Audio remix of “Bareback In Babylon”. Artwork is by Kallisti Design. Welcome To Weimar America by Avarice In Audio “Let The Boreal Burn (v.2026)” reworks a track with longtime collaborator Static Logic, and the closing track remixes “Bareback In Babylon” in the band’s own hands. Alfa Matrix describes the album as the duo’s “most extreme, abrasive and deliberately uncomfortable” record to date, moving away from the darker synth-pop, harsh elektro and EBM of their earlier catalogue. Avarice In Audio’s history on Alfa Matrix Avarice In Audio previously released “Tear Heaven In Half” on Alfa Matrix in October 2024, a 17-track album that folded in Drum ‘n’ Bass, techno and hard-rock elements and featured Static Logic, Canadian artist Virtual Terrorist and Studio-X. Before that came the “Drowning One” EP (September 2024) and the single “Wicked Die Alone” (February 2024). “Welcome To Weimar America” is the duo’s first full album since “Tear Heaven In Half”. About Avarice In Audio Avarice In Audio is an Australian dark electro project built around Gerry Hawkins and Lawrie B, who also records as Studio-X. The band’s fourth album, “From The Rib Of Adam”, preceded a reduction to the current two-person line-up. As a duo, Avarice In Audio released the “The Language Of Violence” EP in June 2022, featuring a remix by aggrotech act Viscera Drip and a version by Studio-X, ahead of the fifth album “Our Idols Are Filth” in October 2022, which included collaborations with iVardensphere and the Italian project T-Error Machinez. The band returned with the “I Pray” EP in February 2021 featuring Assemblage 23’s Tom Shear, and later issued the “War Tanz” EP with an accompanying video in April 2023. “Tear Heaven In Half” followed in October 2024, described by Gerry Hawkins in a Side-Line interview as splitting into a heavier first half and a softer, futurepop-leaning second half. “Welcome To Weimar America” is the band’s seventh studio album and continues the collaboration with Static Logic that ran through “Tear Heaven In Half”.

items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — Dark Asylum by Kamelot is quite possibly the strongest album the band have released since the departure of former vocalist Roy Khan from the band 15 years ago. While vocalist Tommy Karevik is an insane talent, I always found his contributions to the band to either be rather dull or just an impersonation of former vocalist Roy Khan, but on this album he does show alot more personality & nuance, like he did with his previous band Seventh Wonder. While this isn't overly different from what the band usually produce, the songwriting is stronger and the guest vocalists do add extra dimensions to the band's expected gothic prog symphonic power metal. I'd give this a low to mid 7/10. The track I'd recommend is The Sleeping Mind (Orphic Paradigm).

items.body: Review by Matti — Kimmo P�rsti is one of my favourite prog musicians/producers from Finland, and one of the most prolific too. He runs Seacrest Oy, an independent prog label behind The Samurai of Prog, Guildmaster (both having P�rsti in their core team) and naturally his solo albums and collaborations with Rafael Pacha from Spain. This new release from him may not be among my personal favourites, but the cover artist Ed Unitsky has (again!) done excellent work. His fantasy landscapes have never looked better than here.Let's go straight to the reason why my reception for this 63-minute album is rather reserved. The vocalists. Mark Wilkinson (singing on three tracks) represents the Gabriel/Collins/Fish school of prog singers I have grown a bit tired of in the contemporary prog, including the earlier Seacrest releases where Wilkinson has often guested. And Dan Schamber (two tracks, plus one as a backing vocalist), who has written most of the lyrics here, is in my opinion pretty uninspiring as a vocalist. Technically OK, but his expression is sort of flat. Without going into track by track analysis, several songs of this album don't truly impress me emotionally. The best songs, or my personal favourites, are 'In My Life' (originally by Ambrosia?) which is sung by Michael Trew & Steph Honde, and 'The Only One in the Crowd' sung by Wilkinson.Of the 11 tracks (all more or less roughly between 5 and 7 minutes), five are instrumentals. They see to have more variety in moods than the songs. Energetic 'Carrousel', composed by Jean-Pascal Boffo, is focused on dual electric guitars of Toni Jokinen (aka RIVERYMAN) and Pacha, and is slightly reminiscent of Camel. P�rsti's fusion composition 'Things Not Seen' features Risto Salmi on sax and EWI together with Jokinen (g), Jan-Olof Strandberg (b) and P�rsti (dr, keyb). 'Light of Other Days' (P�rsti/Pacha) is beautiful especially due to Hanna P�rsti's flute. The closing piece 'With a Breath I Linger' (P�rsti) is the album's most serene track, a soothing and delicate, slow-tempo piece for flute, classical guitar, double bass and keyboards, the flute dominating.With another kind of cast for vocal duties (sadly no female voices this time!) I would surely enjoy this well produced album more. Anyway, this is yet another fine release keeping up the Seacrest's high standards on both music and the physical package. Easily 4 stars.

items.body: Review by Hrychu — I dunno, but I'm underwhelmed. The album is absolutely fine, but I feel like the music is so ok thatit somehow doesn't leave a trace of a lasting impression on me. I feel like the songwriting isuninspired as hell. It's very "library music". Almost as if the two guys didn't want to but wereforced to record it with a gun pointed to their heads by an IOM executive. I wish there wasexperimentation with the format, more complex guitar playing, more fun to the whole thing,especially knowing that the creators of this albums are none other than two prog guitarists KNOWNfor their virtuoso playing. What the hell happened? Aging? 👴 Anyways, there is some complexityhere, but not enough of it imo. I can maybe pick 2 or 3 moments where Hackett and Rothery are atleast trying to put some effort into their playing, like, in the intro to the title track, but thevast majority of the album, unfortunately, is no better than a random intermediate guitaristnoodling to a backing tack through Amplitube in their bedroom . :\ The album is decent but it'sdefinitely not even close to the quality level that would ever live up to Hackett and/or Rothery. The production, mixing, instrumental playing from Hackett, Rothery and all of the instrumentalists and everything else on the technical side of things is done with competence and professionalism. But the thing is, nothing about this album screams Steve Hackett and Steve Rothery imo. It could be anyone's album. If it was some random newcomer, I'd probably go less harsh and be less disappointed. It's a personal letdown. For me.EDIT: Bumped my score from 2 to 4 stars. I do understand that not everyone is indifferent towards rankings and numeric votes. Take care. Peace. I'm out.

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — Embroiled by turbulence and tragedy, prog sludge metal masters MASTODON have pretty much ruled theroost in one of prog metal's most gritty subgenres throughout the years since the band's inceptionin 2000 having churned out four classics during their first decade run. While the 2010s may haveseen a dip in quality the band stilled sallied forth into battle delivering solid if not perfectprog sludge metal releases but then change tends to rear its ugly head in unexpected ways and shakesthings up dramatically. After 25 years founding member Brent Hinds succumbed to the tensions brewingin the band and decided to leave the band and then even more shocking died in an unfortunatemotorcycle accident soon after. Would MASTODON continue or call it a day? Given the unevenness andcontinuing decline in quality, many including myself thought it was the end. However that was notthe case. The band not only continued but returns in 2026 with its strongest album since "Crack TheSkye."MARROW DEEP is the 9th album by this Atlanta based act and a turning point in the band's history.Stepping in to fill Hinds' shoes is guitarist / vocalist Nick Johnston formerly of Osmanthus andalso added to team is keyboardist Jo�o Nogueira. A new five-piece version of MASTODON is born. Thealbum also features seven guests adding vocals, bass and percussion including Lamb of God's RandyBlythe and Black Sabbath's Geezer Butcher amongst others. Graced with yet another stylish dose ofalbum cover art that never fails to deliver, MARROW DEEP not only is a pretty album to behold butreally does bring the band full circle to the heavy sludge metal leanings that launched them intopopular favor over two decades ago. After a few wimpy albums during the last decade, the shakeupseems to have reinvigorated the band much like the latest from Neurosis and finds the band inexcellent form not only with stronger compositions but also in musical delivery. While nothing isspectacularly new in the MASTODON universe as far as stylistic approach, everything just sounds morepassionately inspired this time around.Known for their long albums, MARROW DEEP is yet another hour plus crossroads where progressivemetal, sludge metal and stoner rock converge to deliver a lethal dose of filthy sonic grit takingthe band back to the days of "Leviathan" and "Blood Mountain" which happen to be my favorite twoalbums by the band so it goes without saying that this is a much welcome reprise in the band's peakperformances of the early 2000s. The album wastes no time declaring MASTODON is back with avengeance with the opening "Barbarian's Blood" which signals the path to 65 1/2 minutes of 12 sludgytracks that deliver all the MASTODON goods in rich abundance. Steeped with dueling guitar grunge,slower contemplative moments that offer dramatic diversity and the band's uncanny progressivemeanderings, MARROW DEEP is like a big boil that popped and covering your senses with grimy oozethat absolutely reeks! You know, the way sludge metal is supposed to slap you in the face!From the bantering opener throughout there are no weak tracks on this one. Technically the last twotracks, two of my faves are the best. "The Vanishing" offers a doomy intro before erupting intofull-fueled sludgery while "The Three Fates" offers a nice jazzy keyboard break from the brashbravado and despite the presence of keys on this release, they remain fairly subdued and almostundetectable save for scant appearances where they stick out. Overall MASTODON threw the ultimatecurveball in 2026 with MARROW DEEP and along with Neurosis proved that old dogs can still learn newtricks although nothing's really substantially new on this release but rather picking up in a waywhere "Crack The Skye" left off and adding the quality control back to the entire album's playingtime. While i wouldn't call this the band's absolute best, i would call it the best since theirfirst four releases. A stellar year for MASTODON fans it is!

items.body:
Music Matters Live is turning 21, and it is marking the milestone with four nights of free live music in Singapore.

Happening from 2 to 4 October and 7 October at CQ @ Clarke Quay, this year's edition will bring together 40 emerging artists from 15 countries, with performances taking place at Fountain Square, Swee Lee, and more venues around CQ @ Clarke Quay.

The lineup includes Lola Amour from the Philippines, KID PHENOMENON from EXILE TRIBE and LIL LEAGUE from Japan, DOLLA from Malaysia, Borderline from New Zealand, Bratty from Mexico, Pierce Brothers and Flynn Gurry from Australia, Singapore's St. Humain, China's Runyu, and more.

Music Matters Live will also host a series of dedicated showcases throughout the week. Universal Music's Music Is Universal returns on 4 October with performances from DOLLA, LYHAN, MARBLES, VVV, and XONARA, bringing together acts from Malaysia, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, and the Philippines.

The festival's MadeIN series will expand with the debut of MadeIN Philippines Spotlight Weekend, presented by NCCA in partnership with BSE and Music Matters. Running from 2 to 4 October, it will feature Filipino acts KAIA, PIX!E, and Lola Amour. MadeIN Japan will bring LIL LEAGUE and KID PHENOMENON to the stage on 3 October, while the inaugural MadeIN Nagaland showcase will spotlight emerging artists from the Indian state.

Meanwhile, Sounds Australia will stage two showcases on 3 and 4 October, featuring Alice George, FVNERAL, Flynn Gurry, Holly Hebe, Lucy Sugerman, Mariae Cassandra, Peach Fuzz, Pierce Brothers, Reuben De Melo, SAHXL, Squid The Kid, and TOWNS.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bandwagon Asia | Music News • Asia Festivals & Artists (@bandwagonasia)

Closing out Music Matters Live on 7 October is Girls' Night Out, presented by It's A Girl Thing and Branded. The showcase will feature Bratty — the festival's first artist from Mexico — alongside Maisha Kanna, Lucy Sugerman, SARINA, Singapore's Haneri on the decks, and more. According to the organisers, around half of this year's lineup is female-led.

Music Matters Live will take place alongside the 21st edition of All That Matters, which runs from 5 to 7 October, and forms part of the Singapore Grand Prix Season.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by All That Matters (@matters.asia)

3 October, 4 PM — Music Matters Live / MadeIN Nagaland / MadeIN Philippines Spotlight / MadeIN Japan, Mainstage at Fountain Square

7 October — Music Matters Live, Swee Lee @ Clarke Quay

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由三位多伦多音乐人远程合作完成，历经多年邮件交流打磨，收录了十八首短小精悍的原创曲目，总时长仅三十四分钟。编曲以原声吉他、尤克里里琴和滑棒吉他为核心，配以清脆的键盘点缀，整体气质偏向简约民谣与美式根源音乐。歌词聚焦于失去、爱情消逝与对世界的无奈接受，歌手嗓音清亮高亢，偶尔流露出脆弱感。作品风格跨度较广，从矿工蓝调、乡村灵魂到多莉·巴顿式的伤感叙事均有涉猎，但整体框架仍属于传统民谣范畴，缺乏显著的实验性或电子元素。专辑给人一种梦境般的朦胧氛围，旋律优美却未走向前卫方向，对偏好实验、前卫或电子音乐的听众而言，这张专辑的吸引力较为有限。
